properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 20 at 10:26PM EST until November 21 at 12:30AM EST by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
FFWJAX

The National Weather Service in Jacksonville has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southwestern Gilchrist County in northern Florida...

* Until 1230 AM EST.

* At 1026 PM EST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2.5 and 5 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 1.5 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Trenton.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall has maintained a steady climb into Moderate Flood
Stage on the St Johns River at Deland, with river levels forecast to
continue climbing through next week. The river is anticipated to
reach Major Flood Stage this weekend, with additional rises
thereafter.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EST Friday the stage was 5.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EST Friday was 5.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 6.0 feet early next
week. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday afternoon at noon EST.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 20 at 9:59PM AST until November 21 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...High Rip Current Risk, life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE...From Rincon to Fajardo

* WHEN...Through Saturday afternoon

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

and Redbug Alley on the north bank of the North Fork. Flooding
begins at Enchanted Lane on the south bank of the North Fork. At
16.0 feet, Flooding expands into the yards of more properties along
Lazy Acres Road on the north bank of the North Fork. Flooding
begins further downstream of the Blanding Blvd Bridge along North
and South Lee. Flooding begins on areas of the south bank of the
North Fork, particularly at Scenic Drive and Enchanted Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 15.0 feet
tomorrow evening.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 20 at 2:52PM PST until November 26 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 3.0 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National
Seashore, San Francisco Peninsula Coast, Northern Monterey Bay
and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Saturday to 4 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 8:15 AM
Saturday, 2.1 ft above normal (7.9 ft MLLW) at 8:48 AM Sunday,
2.3 ft above normal (8.1 ft MLLW) at 9:25 AM Monday, 2.9 ft
above normal (8.7 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 3.0 ft above
normal (8.8 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.6 ft above
normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions
include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical
tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes
earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San
Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 20 at 12:26PM PST until November 21 at 10:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High astronomical tides
will cause minor flooding in low lying areas around Humboldt
Bay. Up to one half foot of saltwater inundation above ground
level is possible near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the
Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf may
cause major flooding in low lying areas along the
Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to 2.5 to 3 feet of saltwater
inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways during the highest tides if
storm impacts such as strong southerly winds and large surf
arrive during high tide periods.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County, especially for areas in
and around Humboldt Bay.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 7 AM to 10 AM PST
Saturday with high tide at 8:31 AM on Saturday at the Humboldt
Bay North Spit tide gauge. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from
Sunday morning through Thursday afternoon. High tide is at
9:06 AM on Sunday, 9:44 AM on Monday, 10:25 AM on Tuesday,
11:09 AM on Wednesday, 11:56 AM on Thursday, 12:48 AM on
Friday at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater
inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high
tide.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
Some shoreline erosion may occur.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Watch means that flooding is possible but not
imminent. Coastal residents in the watch area should begin
preparations for rising water and take appropriate action to
protect life and property.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding expected. For the
Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible.

especially around the time of high tide, including over

possible. There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and Thursday
with potential for significant impacts. Additional products
will likely be needed into Friday.
.

in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
and breaking waves due to elevated surf. Elevated to high surf
will likely continue into much of next week. For the Coastal
Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding expected. For the
Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible.

* WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.Impacts
highest across west-facing beaches, including from Santa Monica
to Palos Verdes. In addition, the Long Beach/Naples area will be
susceptible to the very high water levels.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 3 PM PST this
afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to
3 AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late
Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of
sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas,
especially around the time of high tide, including over
beaches, roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is
possible. There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and Thursday
with potential for significant impacts. Additional products
will likely be needed into Friday.
.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Plan
for extra travel time as some roads may be closed.

Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

properties.areaDesc: Columbia River Bar
properties.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued November 20 at 12:03PM PST until November 22 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Rough bar conditions expected. Seas 7 to 12 ft at 14
seconds and southeast winds 10 to 20 kt with gusts up to 25 kt
expected.

* WHERE...In the Main Channel of the Columbia River Bar.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Saturday to 4 AM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft,
especially when operating near to, or attempting to cross, the
Columbia River Bar.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Ebb current of 4.59 kt at 110 PM Friday.
Seas 7 to 6 ft. Ebb current of 3.26 kt at 123 AM Saturday. Seas
7 to 6 ft. Ebb current of 5.44 kt at 154 PM Saturday. Seas 10
ft.
properties.instruction:
A Small Craft Advisory means that wave conditions are expected to
be hazardous to small craft in the vicinity of the Columbia River
Bar. Mariners are advised to obtain the latest bar conditions
from the United States Coast Guard before attempting to cross the
bar.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 20 at 1:00PM MST until November 24 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...
Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 100 PM MST, water releases from Painted Rock Dam continue with
flow peaking around 3000 cfs. A streamflow gauge immediately
downstream also indicated a stage near 10 feet.
- Flooding is expected along the Gila River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 20 at 10:56AM PST until November 24 at 4:00AM PST by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal
flooding possible.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4 AM
PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from 4 AM PST Tuesday
through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Morning high tides will be on the increase
next week, exceeding 7 feet by Sunday. Highest tides will be
Tuesday through Thursday, peaking Wednesday. Daily high tides
each morning on Tuesday through Thursday will reach 7.9-8.2
feet. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 3-5
feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday into
Thursday could bring notably higher surf beginning on Thursday.
NOTE: Tides have been adjusted above baseline astronomical
predictions based on trends in recent observations.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Flagler County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 7 AM EST Sunday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Dangerous
swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
properties.instruction:

travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:

* WHERE...Franklin County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through late Friday night.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 20 at 12:58AM EST until November 22 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents and
rough surf. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of
5 to 12 feet in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday evening.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.
